title: Galileo Galilei
passages: Galileo Galilei was born on 15 February 1564 in Pisa, a city in Italy famous for its leaning bell tower. His father, Vincenzo, was a musician who liked to test ideas with careful experiments, and young Galileo picked up that habit. He first studied medicine, but mathematics soon pulled him away. In 1609, when he was 45, he heard that SPECTACLE makers in the Netherlands had put two glass lenses in a tube to make faraway things look closer. Dutch towns were busy trading ports full of skilled glass workers, and their clever idea spread quickly across Europe. Galileo decided to build his own.

His first telescope made things look about 3 times bigger, but he kept grinding better lenses until one reached nearly 20 times. When he turned it to the night sky, the ASTRONOMER saw mountains and CRATERS on the Moon. On 7 January 1610 he spotted small points of light beside Jupiter, and within about a week he realized that four moons were circling it. Today we call them Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. He also found that the Milky Way holds countless faint stars, and later in 1610 he watched Venus show PHASES, just like our Moon. In March 1610 he shared his findings in a short book of only about 60 pages.
